Block-Paving Driveways in Pinner

Pinner has a character all of its own, from the historic High Street with its timber-framed buildings to the leafy roads around Pinner Memorial Park and Pinner Hill. A driveway that suits your Pinner home

Pinner has a wide range of houses:

  • 1930s semi-detached houses around Rayners Lane, Pinner Green and North Harrow, where the front garden is often converted to parking.
  • Larger detached homes towards Pinner Hill and Hatch End, where a wider driveway may need to fit several cars and a turning space.
  • Older period properties near the village centre, where a more traditional look often suits best.

Block paving works well for all of these, because you can choose colours and laying patterns to match the house [PLACEHOLDER: confirm range of colours/patterns offered]. We use quality materials, including Marshalls bricks.

Local things to think about

  • Harrow Council: Pinner is in the London Borough of Harrow. A new or wider dropped kerb usually needs the council's approval [PLACEHOLDER: confirm what help you offer with dropped-kerb applications].
  • Conservation areas: Pinner has several conservation areas, including the High Street and parts of the surrounding roads [PLACEHOLDER: confirm conservation-area wording]. If your home is in one, check any extra rules before changing the front garden.
  • Larger and sloping plots: Some Pinner driveways are long or sit on a slope. We plan levels and edges carefully so the finished drive looks neat and works well day to day.
